# GitHub username binding and the access preview

An agent can be bound to a GitHub username, and an admin can preview which repositories that account can reach. The binding is **identity only**: it names the GitHub account whose repository access Sync compares the agent's repos and installation against ([`github-enterprise-apps.md`](./github-enterprise-apps.md#sync)). The binding itself enforces nothing, and no token or credential is stored with it. The preview is read-only. This page covers the binding, who may set it and why, how it differs from `ownerEmail` and `AgentMember`, the preview, and how to read its results. It builds on the optional lookup App described in [`github-enterprise-apps.md`](./github-enterprise-apps.md). File map: [`agent-key-files.md`](./agent-key-files.md).

## The binding

`Agent.githubUsername` is a nullable, non-unique column (several agents may name the same account). It is stored lower-cased. Set or clear it with `PATCH /agents/{id}` (a string, or `null` to clear) or from the agent detail page ("Owner & identities" card, GitHub username row). Syntax is validated only (1-39 letters, digits and single hyphens, no leading or trailing hyphen) and GitHub is never called when saving; an invalid login is a `422`. Existence is checked only by the preview.

## Who can set it, and why

**Platform admin only.** Session members, `platform.ops` keys and agent keys all get `403`.

The reason is that the platform does not verify that a username belongs to the caller. Because the bound account decides which repos the Sync strips from an agent, letting anyone bind any username would let them borrow another account's access. So only a platform admin, who is trusted to bind the right account, may do it.

Operational rule: **agents must not hold the `*` admin key.** An agent holding `*` is a platform admin and could rebind itself to a more privileged GitHub account. Agent credentials stay per-agent bearer tokens, which cannot call the binding.

The route logs the caller name and the agent id only.

## Not the same as `ownerEmail` or `AgentMember`

Three similar-looking fields answer different questions:

| Field | What it is | Verified? | Used for |
|-------|------------|-----------|----------|
| `ownerEmail` | Who created the agent (the creating caller's email). | No: unverified metadata. | Tracing an agent to its per-agent Anthropic identity. Not an access control. |
| `AgentMember` rows | The email access list: the humans allowed to use the agent (for example when `restrictSlackToMembers` is on). | Emails come from sign-in or admin entry. | Who may talk to and manage the agent. |
| `githubUsername` | The GitHub account whose push access the Sync checks the agent's repos against. | No, which is why it is admin-only. | Repo scope only. |

Changing one never changes the others.

## The preview

`GET /agents/{id}/github-access` returns what the bound account can reach: `404` for an unknown agent, `422` when no username is bound, and platform admin only. It uses the lookup App, across the orgs the installer App can install on. If the enterprise Apps are not configured the status is `unconfigured` and GitHub is not called; a login that does not exist on GitHub returns `user_not_found`. The full response shape is in [`agent-api-resources.md`](./agent-api-resources.md#preview-access).

On the agent detail page, admins with the enterprise Apps configured see the GitHub username row and a **Preview access** card that lists reachable repos per org. Responses and logs never contain tokens or keys.

## Levels: what can push

Each repo carries the level GitHub returned for the user:

| Level | Can push |
|-------|----------|
| `admin` | yes |
| `maintain` | yes |
| `write` | yes |
| `triage` | no |
| `read` | no |
| `none` | no |

`canPush` is true for the first three only. `none` is an explicit answer from GitHub that the user has no access.

## Unknown is never none

A repo that could not be checked is **not** reported as `none`. It is left out of `repos` and counted in `unresolved`. A partial or rate-limited result therefore means "not resolved", never "no access". Read the per-org `status` and the top-level `complete` flag:

- `complete` is true only when the user exists, was verified and every org is `ok`.
- `partial`: some repos resolved, others did not (a rate limit, a 403 or a per-repo failure stopped the rest), OR the lookup App is installed on selected repositories only.
- `rate_limited`: nothing resolved because GitHub rate-limited the lookup.
- `lookup_app_not_installed`: the lookup App is not installed on that org.
- `error`: the org could not be read for another reason.

Anything built on this data, including the Sync, must treat unresolved repos as unknown and never as denied or as granted.
